[[File:Kawara-jinja (Geku) 02.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Sacred grove of Kawara Shrine and Mori Shrine]]
'''{{ill|Kawara Shrine (Geku)|ja|河原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawara Shrine (Geku)|qq=}}''' (*Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. This article also covers the '''{{ill|Mori Shrine|ja|毛理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 河原神社 (伊勢市)|1=Kawara Shrine (Geku)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228197}}''' (*Mori Jinja*), which is enshrined alongside Kawara Shrine.
== Overview ==
The shrine is located in Misato-cho Shinkai, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}, enshrined in a forest surrounded by {{ill|rice paddies|ja|水田|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/rice paddies|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 田|1=Paddy field|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q842623}} to the north of {{ill|Garyūbai Park|ja|臥竜梅公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Garyūbai Park|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, known for its connection to {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}} and the Garyūbai plum tree<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 45</ref>.
Like {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawarabuchi Shrine|qq=}}, which is also an auxiliary shrine of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|lt=Kōtai Jingū|lt=Outer Shrine|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮}}, and {{ill|Mori Shrine|ja|毛理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 河原神社 (伊勢市)|1=Kawara Shrine (Geku)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17228197}}, which is enshrined together with Kawara Shrine, the three are collectively known as the "Mitsu-sha" (Three Shrines). According to ancient texts, Kawara Shrine is located north of Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy1">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 911</ref>. Some theories suggest that Kawara Shrine was originally situated at the site of Hinokijiri Shrine along the Hinokijiri River in {{ill|Funae, Ise|ja|船江 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Funae, Ise|1=Funae|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17213313}}, but during the Edo period, when Kawarabuchi Shrine was restored, Hinokijiri Shrine was identified with Kawarabuchi Shrine's site. As a result, Kawara Shrine was reconstructed further north in Misato-cho Shinkai, Ise<ref name="uy1"/>.
== Kawara Shrine ==
Kawara Shrine Ranks 11th among the 16 auxiliary shrines of the Outer Shrine. Its {{ill|Saijin|lt=Saijin|lt=Enshrined deity|ja|Kami|lt=Kami|lt=Deity|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/enshrined deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミ}} is the {{ill|River deity|ja|川神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/River deity|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135579704}}<ref name="ic"/>. The deity serves as the {{ill|Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deities|lt=Guardian deity|ja|守護神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guardian deity|qq=}} of the lower reaches of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River|1=Miya River (Mie)}} and also protects the rice fields<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 63</ref>.
Although the enshrined deity of the former site of Hinokijiri Shrine in Funae, Ise, was unknown, it was decided to enshrine the River deity from Kawara Shrine due to its historical connection<ref name="uy4">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 914</ref>. Hinokijiri Shrine was relocated to the same site as Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy4"/>.
== Mori Shrine ==
Mori Shrine Ranks 6th among the 8 subsidiary shrines of the Outer Shrine. Its enshrined deity is the {{ill|Tree deity|ja|木神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tree deity|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135579705}}<ref name="ic"/>. This deity is regarded as the spirit of the {{ill|Shinboku|en|Shinboku|qid=Q48743901|lt=sacred tree|1=Shinboku}} in the forest where the shrine is located<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>.
It is believed that the site of Mori Shrine corresponds to the former location of Shigai Shrine in Misato-cho Shinkai<ref name="uy2">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol. 2, p. 912</ref>. Shigai Shrine was later relocated to the same site as Kawarabuchi Shrine<ref name="uy4"/>.
== History ==
According to the definition of Ise Jingū's subsidiary shrines, Mori Shrine was established before the compilation of the {{ill|Enryaku Gishikichō|lt=Enryaku Gishikichō|lt=Enryaku Gishiki-chō|ja|延暦儀式帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enryaku Gishiki-chō|qq=}}, i.e., before {{ill|Enryaku|en|Enryaku|qid=Q1373176|lt=Enryaku|1=Enryaku}} 23 (804). Based on the definition of auxiliary shrines, Kawara Shrine was established before the compilation of the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, i.e., before {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|1=Enchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97379316}} 5 (927)<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 22</ref>. 
During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=medieval period|1=Middle Ages}}, rituals were discontinued, and by the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|qid=Q5308718|lt=early modern period|1=Early modern period}}, the shrine sites had become unknown. In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun|1=Kanbun (era)}} 3 (1663), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河辺精長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawabe Masanaga|1=Kiyonaga Kawabe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q92924151}} (also known as Ōnakatomi Masanaga) restored the shrines at their current locations<ref>Furan Ken, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20150610132106/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/ise/bun/is080144-01.html Kawara Shrine]" (Accessed September 29, 2013)</ref>.
== Flora ==
A large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=camphor tree|1=Camphora officinarum}} stands behind the {{ill|shrine building|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shrine building|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|1=Shinto architecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}}<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/>. The {{ill|sacred precinct|ja|神域|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sacred precinct|1=shin'iki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588853}} is well-maintained with neatly trimmed hedges<ref name="ic"/>.
== Access and Surroundings ==
Next to Kawara Shrine and Mori Shrine is a {{ill|Factory|en|Factory|qid=Q83405|lt=factory|1=Factory}} operated by Matsuya Confectionery, known for producing black candy<ref>Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 49</ref>. A 10-minute walk north along Ise City Road will lead to the site of the former {{ill|Yamada Magistrate's Office|ja|山田奉行所|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Magistrate's Office|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山田奉行|1=Yamada bugyō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4275043}}<ref name="gk"/>.
* About a 6-minute walk (approx. 500 m) from the "Shinkai" {{ill|Bus stop|en|Bus stop|qid=Q953806|lt=bus stop|1=Bus stop}} serviced by {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu|1=Mie Kotsu}} buses.
* Approximately a 2-minute drive (approx. 800 m) north from the "Ogicho 1" {{ill|Intersection (road)|en|Intersection (road)|qid=Q285783|lt=intersection|1=Intersection (road)}} on {{ill|Japan National Route 23|en|Japan National Route 23|qid=Q5357579|lt=National Route 23|1=Japan National Route 23}} ({{ill|Nansei Bypass|ja|南勢バイパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nansei Bypass|1=Q11407535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11407535}}). No parking is available nearby.
